The petitioner was working as a Senior Sales Officer, in Karnataka Agro-Chemicals.
He submitted a resignation letter on 19.10.2012 to the company.
However, this resignation is stated to have been rejected on 26.10.2012.

2. The learned counsel for the petitioner points out that a show-cause notice was issued to the petitioner on 27.11.2012 in the following terms:
NC: 2024:KHC:20922 "Date:27.11.2012 Bangalore To, Mr.Shivaji Vishwasrao Sangle Senior Sales Officer, Pune Branch
Dear Mr.S.V.Sangle, Sub:-Show Cause notice for misappropriation of company funds and vehicle REF: 1. YOUR RESIGNATION LETTER DATED 19.10.2012
2. OUR LETTER No.KAR/HR/LT/06/20012-13 DATED 26.10.2012

We have replied to your resignation letter dated 19.10.2012 vide our letter dated 26.10.2012 and we have clearly intimated that you will not relieved from our service and your resignation letter has been rejected.

However, we wish to state as under:

sentences.text: It was alleged that every month he was attending the monthly Performance Review Meeting and he was in the habit of misbehaving with the senior staff and also using abusive language in front of the other staff apart from harassing junior staff.

6. It was alleged that he had started spreading false messages about the Company and its products and was also refusing to collect the outstanding dues from the customers and advising them not to settle their dues and he was therefore trying to tarnish the image of the Company.
7. It was lastly alleged that he had joined a competitor company called M/s.Green crop International Private NC: 2024:KHC:20922 Limited from 27.08.2012 and was drawing salary etc., from them.

sentences.text:
8. It was also contended that he had committed lakhs of rupees and made offers to retailers,
distributors and dealers, which he was not authorized to make, due to which the Company suffered huge amounts of loss and therefore, the action was required to be taken.
9.
On the basis of this complaint, the Police registered an FIR under Sections 420, 504 and 506 of IPC.

Thereafter, the Police have proceeded to lay a charge- sheet, in which it was principally contended that the petitioner had been provided with a Bolero car and without appointing a driver,
he had been drawing a salary.

It is also alleged that the petitioner had not collected the outstanding dues from the dealers and had joined a competitor's Company and was securing salary from his original Company and his newly joined Company and this amounted to an offence under Section 420 of IPC.

A reading of the show-cause notice, which was issued to the petitioner after he had submitted his resignation, clearly goes to show that the essential dispute that the Company had was regarding the resignation of the petitioner.

The fact that the resignation was rejected, and thereafter, a show-cause notice was issued and this was followed up by lodging a Police complaint, fundamentally indicates that the Company was going after the petitioner only because he had decided to quit the services of the Company.

11. Even if all the allegations in the charge-sheet are accepted to be true, they would only amount to a violation of the terms of the service conditions and cannot be construed as the petitioner having committed a crime, for which he was liable to be prosecuted on the criminal side.
12. Therefore, I am of the view that there is no justification to continue the proceedings as against the petitioner.
The impugned proceedings are therefore quashed.
The petition is accordingly allowed.
